solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Large canine ostracised with regard to smell

indicators.note: someone ostracised is shut out of the group, so a letter is cast out of the word

parts.note: cosmic means vast, on the scale of the universe
C is the dental abbreviation for a canine tooth

explanation.surface: A big dog shunned by the pack because of how it smells.
explanation.walkthrough: COSMIC loses its C to leave OSMIC. 'Large canine' reads as one big dog, but the adjective and the noun are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmic is a technical adjective meaning relating to odours or the sense of smell.

clue.text: Rare pretentious shows seen in huge temporary accommodation

parts.note: OS stands for outsize
tents are shelters put up for a short stay

explanation.surface: Showy displays put on in an enormous marquee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' belongs to the definition, flagging a rarely used word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostent is a rare noun for an ostentatious display or show.

clue.text: Check family in Bow

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stop or hold back a flow
second meaning: a line of descent or ancestry
third meaning: the front part of a ship

explanation.walkthrough: Bow reads as the East London district, but it is the front of a ship. Three meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: One short word means to staunch, a family stock, and the post at a ship's prow.

clue.text: Small clues improved becoming very small

indicators.note: improved means reworked, so the letters are put into a better order

parts.note: mini means small
the five letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: Tiny crossword clues have been sharpened up.
explanation.walkthrough: MINISCULE is a recognised variant spelling of minuscule.
explanation.definitionFit: Minuscule means extremely tiny, from Latin minusculus, rather small.

clue.text: Contract to organise and look after old defensive armour

indicators.note: to contract is to shrink, so the word is shortened by its tail

parts.note: to curate a collection is to select, arrange and care for it

explanation.surface: A deal to manage and maintain a collection of old armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun, an agreement; it is a verb telling you to shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: Curat is an obsolete form of cuirass, a breastplate worn for protection.

clue.text: Real lead in fuel not imaginary

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is wanted

parts.note: first letter of fuel
what is actual exists and is not imagined

explanation.surface: A claim about real lead in petrol, insisting it is no fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Real lead' suggests leaded fuel; Real is the definition and 'lead in' picks one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Factual describes something based on facts, i.e. genuine and true rather than invented.

clue.text: Clowns on stage leading to mad excitement

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: a flat is an old word for a dupe or simpleton
a stage of a journey is a leg, and pin is slang for leg

explanation.surface: Clowns on stage whip the audience into a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On stage' suggests a theatre; stage is a leg of a journey, and pins are legs.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a flat spin is an idiom for a state of agitated panic or frantic excitement.

clue.text: Check on, for instance, man's familiar name

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: CH is chess notation for check
as means for instance, as in such as

explanation.surface: Verifying, say, what a man is called by his friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Chas is the common informal short form of Charles, a pet name.

clue.text: Monkey sitting on date tree abroad

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a tamarin is a small South American monkey
D abbreviates date

explanation.surface: A monkey perched on a date palm in a foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Date tree' suggests the palm; the date is a calendar one.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarind is a tropical leguminous tree, native to Africa and grown in hot countries.

clue.text: Inability to recognise familiar things again? So unsettling

indicators.note: something unsettled is disturbed, its letters knocked out of place

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Failing to know familiar things a second time is upsetting.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnosia is a neurological loss of the ability to identify objects, people or sounds.

clue.text: Scottish lovers banking nothing very much

indicators.note: banking means putting away safely inside, so one word holds another

parts.note: in Scots a lad is a sweetheart
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Scottish couples putting away no savings at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Loads is informal for a great deal, as in thanks loads.

clue.text: Tulips finished by end of June showing leafy appendage

indicators.note: flowers that are finished are spent and wrecked, so their letters fall into a new order
followed by: the next piece is placed straight after the first

parts.note: the six letters of the flower name, rearranged

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: last letter of June

explanation.surface: Garden tulips have gone over by late June, leaving only leaves to show.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram covers only the flower's letters; the E is added afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipule is a small leaf-like outgrowth at the base of a leaf stalk, a botanical appendage.

clue.text: Ship slowly heading off

indicators.note: the head of the word is taken off, so its first letter goes

parts.note: largo is the musical direction for a slow, broad tempo

explanation.surface: A vessel moving off at a gentle pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' reads as setting sail, but it removes the L from LARGO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo is the legendary vessel in which Jason and the Argonauts sailed for the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: One's behind teacher sharing mischievous grounds for complaint

indicators.note: placed behind means coming after the rest in the word
one word shares the space of another by sitting inside it

parts.note: gamin, from the street urchin, describes an impish, mischievous manner
a rav is a rabbi, a Jewish teacher
A means one; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone stands behind a teacher who is in on a prank, giving cause for complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Gamin, usually a noun for a street urchin, is here the adjective for impish. Gravamina is the Latin plural of gravamen.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravamen is the essential part of a grievance or accusation; the plural names several grievances.

clue.text: Airline angry about spaces quantified? The opposite

indicators.note: one word goes around the other, enclosing it
reverses the stated relation, so the outer word becomes the inner one

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit for measuring space
irate means very angry

explanation.surface: An airline passenger furious at how legroom has been measured out.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, IRATE would surround EMS; 'The opposite' flips it so EMS surrounds IRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Emirates is the Dubai-based international carrier, a well-known airline.

clue.text: Reckless lad stepped into Rhodes almost drunk

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
one word goes into another, landing inside it
drunk means reeling, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: the island name without its final letter
trod is the past of tread, to step

explanation.surface: A young tearaway wandered drunkenly onto a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot-rodder drives a souped-up car fast, typically a reckless young man.

clue.text: Native repelled by hotel meals

definitions.note: a mass noun for food, standing in for the plural

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back the way it came

parts.note: a native of a place is its son, as in native son
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A local turning his nose up at hotel food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is just a word for a son of a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for food or a meal.

clue.text: Desperately determined underworld criminal

parts.note: hell is the underworld of the dead
bent is British slang for corrupt or criminal

explanation.surface: A gangster desperate to get his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld criminal' reads as one gangster, but it splits into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell-bent means recklessly set on doing something whatever the cost.

clue.text: Indian occupying hospital room in the back

indicators.note: something occupying a space is inside it

parts.note: H for hospital and a ward as a hospital room
IND abbreviates Indian

explanation.surface: An Indian patient taking up a bed on a hospital ward at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindward is an old word for towards the rear, related to hind meaning back.

clue.text: Refuse bed with Rector in it

indicators.note: with something in it means holding it inside

parts.note: a doss is a rough bed for the night
R abbreviates rector

explanation.surface: A clergyman turning down a bed because he is already lying in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, to decline; it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is worthless waste matter, rubbish, so it is the noun refuse.

clue.text: Drinking song cheers one getting drunk

parts.note: skol is a Scandinavian drinking toast
Roman numeral one
on can mean tipsy, as in well on

explanation.surface: A song for drinking, toasting one person as they get merry.
explanation.definitionFit: A skolion was a song sung in turn by guests at an ancient Greek banquet over wine.

clue.text: Wreck conceals one in command of rock

indicators.note: what conceals something keeps it hidden inside

parts.note: to spill is to upset or wreck, as of a spilt tray
Roman numeral one
IC is the abbreviation for in charge or in command

explanation.surface: A shipwreck hides the officer in charge of a rocky coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Spilitic is the adjective from spilite, a kind of altered basalt, so it means relating to that rock.

clue.text: Traders in petitions caught for parking

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter swaps in where another stood

parts.note: prayers are petitions to God
C is cricket shorthand for caught
P is the sign for parking

explanation.surface: Merchants bring petitions about being caught for parking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traders' suggests merchants; a crayer is a ship that carries trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayer was a small trading vessel, so crayers are traders in the sense of ships.

clue.text: Useless types spun silk clumsily

indicators.note: done clumsily, the letters are fumbled into a different order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Inept workers made a mess of spinning silk.
explanation.definitionFit: Skulpin, a variant of sculpin, is a worthless fish and so in Chambers a good-for-nothing person.

clue.text: Fees opening around a pound rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back the way it came
one word sits around another, enclosing it

parts.note: a slot is a narrow opening
L, from Latin libra, is a pound

explanation.surface: A charge for a coin slot taking a pound is refused.
explanation.walkthrough: A second L joins the L of SLOT, giving SLLOT, which is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolls are charges paid for using a road, bridge or service.

clue.text: Fish near danger one's avoided

parts.note: to can mean close, as when a door is pushed to

indicators.note: what is avoided is kept out, so that letter is left out

parts.note: risk means danger
Roman numeral one, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A fish close to danger has managed to escape it.
explanation.definitionFit: The torsk is a North Atlantic food fish of the cod family, also called the cusk.

clue.text: Native type American in a home?

indicators.note: something in a place is enclosed within it

parts.note: crib is slang for one's home
A abbreviates American

explanation.surface: A sort of native American, living at home perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native type American' reads as a single phrase, but American is wordplay only.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribs are an indigenous people of the southern Caribbean islands and nearby coast.

clue.text: Capital place once had to be closed early

indicators.note: closing early cuts something short, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: do once meant to put or place, an archaic sense
taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A town that once had to shut early.
explanation.walkthrough: HAD loses its D. 'Once' marks the old sense of do; it is not a time marker.
explanation.definitionFit: Doha is the capital city of Qatar.

clue.text: Evasive about minor league being short of balls

indicators.note: one word wraps about the others, enclosing them

parts.note: coy means reluctant to give details, evasive
a ward is a minor under a guardian
L abbreviates league

explanation.surface: A minor-league sports club dodging questions when it runs out of balls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor league' reads as one sporting phrase but splits into two pieces. 'Balls' is slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking balls is slang for lacking nerve, which is exactly what cowardly means.

clue.text: Review of Stir Crazy partly written up

indicators.note: in a down clue, written upwards means read from bottom to top
only part of the words is used, a run of letters within them

parts.note: a run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A critic's piece on the film Stir Crazy, part of a written write-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir Crazy is a 1980 comedy film; its title hides the letters running backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A crit is informal shorthand for a critique or critical review.

clue.text: Acclaim type of carriage-way erected

indicators.note: something erected is stood upright, so in a down clue it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: a dual carriageway is a divided road

explanation.surface: Praise for a road layout that has been put up.
explanation.walkthrough: A dual carriageway is the British term for a divided highway.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud is to praise highly, a synonym of acclaim.

clue.text: Elder twigs right mind for elaborate composition

parts.note: rice is an old dialect word for twigs or brushwood
R abbreviates right
to mind is to care, take heed

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut elder twigs on the right, take care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elder' means older, marking an old word, not the elder tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A ricercare is an intricate contrapuntal instrumental piece, an early form of fugue.

clue.text: Broadcast very weak on term in prison

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece goes on after the other

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
W abbreviates weak

indicators.note: a term is an end or limit, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the terminal letter of prison

explanation.surface: A very feeble report of someone serving time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Term in prison' looks like a sentence served; term means end, picking out one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcast as a past participle means scattered widely, as seed is sown.

clue.text: Stylist regrets returning after a day

indicators.note: placed after means coming second in the word

parts.note: FRI is the abbreviation for Friday

indicators.note: returning goes back the way it came, so the word reads right to left

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A hairdresser feeling remorse coming back after a day off.
explanation.definitionFit: A friseur is a hairdresser, from French friser, to curl.

clue.text: Tied King's Head mentioned — about time

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of King

indicators.note: one word goes about another, surrounding it

parts.note: something noted has been remarked on
T abbreviates time

explanation.surface: A pub, the King's Head, has been mentioned as tied, a time-related matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The King's Head is a common British pub name, and a tied house is a pub bound to one brewery.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotted means fastened with a knot, i.e. tied.

clue.text: Special on beat turned back old ladies

indicators.note: turned back means facing the other way, so the letters are read in reverse
one piece goes on beside the next, joined end to end

parts.note: S abbreviates special
to drub is to beat thoroughly

explanation.surface: A special constable on the beat sends some elderly women home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On beat' suggests a police officer's round; beat is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Burd is an old Scots and poetic word for a lady or maiden.
